document.title: Time-Space Lower Bounds for Finding Collisions in Merkle-Damgard Hash Functions

candidate.title: A Tight Quantum Time-Space Tradeoff for Two-Block Merkle-Damgard Collisions
candidate.subtitle: Is the known quantum preprocessing attack optimal at two blocks?
candidate.one_line: Whether the best known quantum preprocessing attack, of advantage ST^2/N + T^3/N, is optimal for finding two-block Merkle-Damgard collisions with S qubits of advice and T quantum queries.
candidate.status_note: Nothing is settled: the paper reports that in the quantum setting 'no matching bounds are known, even for B = 2 and B = T'. The classical analogue is settled at Theta-tilde(ST/N + T^2/N). The paper poses this as a question and takes no position.
candidate.progress_note: The paper reports a quantum attack of advantage ST^2/N + T^3/N for every 2 <= B <= T and a security bound it attributes to GLLZ21 and writes as ST^3/N, a factor of about S apart. It offers no partial quantum result of its own.
risks: The quantum model is not defined in the source paper, which is classical throughout; the page's Definition 3 supplies the standard reading and flags it as the part most needing a check against CGLQ20 and GLLZ21.

The paper prints the known bound as Omega(ST^3/N) and the known attack as O(ST^2/N + T^3/N), inverting the usual convention; the figures are quoted as printed and the conjecture is stated in the conventional direction.
The paper asks a question; fixing the affirmative direction is a reading, flagged in a remark.
The related security-jump question is deliberately not merged into this statement.

grounding.quote: Motivated by analyzing post-quantum non-uniform security, several recent works [CGLQ20, GLLZ21] studied the same question in the quantum setting, in which the adversary is given S-(qu)bit of advice and T quantum oracle queries.
However, unlike the classical setting, no matching bounds are known, even for B = 2 and B = T .

Is there a security jump for finding 2-block collisions and unbounded collisions in the quantum setting? Can we leverage our new proof for B = 2 to prove a tight security bound in the quantum setting?
However, the best-known attack achieves O(ST 2 /N + T 3 /N ) for every 2
security bound by [GLLZ21], suggests that the optimal attack may speed up the trivial quantum collision finding by a factor of S.
In particular, their bound confirms STB conjecture for B = O(1).

verify.reason: The question is posed in the paper's 'Discussions and open problems' section and nothing in the paper or the literature settles it. The serious weakness is definitional rather than mathematical: the paper never defines the quantum model, so the statement supplies it, and that is flagged as the reviewer's first job. The paper's inverted O/Omega notation is reproduced rather than repaired.

checks.finding: Posed in section 1.3 under the heading 'Tight quantum time-space tradeoffs for finding collisions in MD?', p. 10.

The paper is classical throughout (its own theorems are Theorems 1-3 and sections 3-4 in the classical AI-ROM); it reports the quantum state of the art as having no matching bounds at any B, and offers no quantum result. Nothing later in the paper touches it.

The paper asks whether a tight bound can be proved; it does not name the tight value. The statement fixes the affirmative direction, taking the reported best attack as optimal. Remark rem:direction records that this is a reading and that refutation resolves the paper's question equally.

The paper writes the known security bound as Omega(ST^3/N) and the known attack as O(ST^2/N + T^3/N), which inverts the usual convention and cannot be resolved from this paper alone. Both figures are quoted as printed in remark rem:notation, the conjecture is stated in the conventional direction, and the reader is told to check GLLZ21 directly.

The question is the source paper's; the quantum attack and the ST^3/N bound are attributed to CGLQ20 and GLLZ21 as the paper attributes them, the classical B=2 result to ACDW20 and the paper's own Theorem 2, and the unbounded-length classical result to CDGS18.

The paper defines only the classical game (Definitions 2-3, p. 12) and describes the quantum setting in one clause. The statement's Definition 3 follows the paper's classical definitions on the classical parts and supplies quantum advice, one unbounded preprocessing stage and standard XOR-type superposition queries. Remark rem:model states that each of these is a choice and names it as the part most in need of checking against CGLQ20 and GLLZ21.

The first draft merged the paper's two quantum questions - the tight B=2 bound and the existence of a security jump - into one statement. Corrected: the statement is only the former, and remark rem:jump explains why granting it would not settle the latter.
Definitions 1-2 plus the notation list fix the construction, the resources and the quantity, subject to the model caveat in rem:model.

corrections.applied: statement restricted to the tight B=2 bound; remark rem:jump separates the security-jump question
